Text: "CNN announces on social media that President Donald Trump dies from COVID-19."
Claim author: Keon & Kavon
Claim date: October 13, 2020
Claim origin: https://web.archive.org/web/20201029171702/https://www.instagram.com/p/CGRMDzhgv9o/?utm_source=ig_embed
before_justification: The claim is refuted because no official CNN social media account announced President Trump's death, and the [archived Instagram post](https://web.archive.org/web/20201029171702/https://www.instagram.com/p/CGRMDzhgv9o/?utm_source=ig_embed) is fabricated, as confirmed by [CNN's October 2020 sitemap](https://edition.cnn.com/article/sitemap-2020-10.html). Furthermore, Trump was alive and publicly active after October 13, 2020, having returned to the White House from Walter Reed on October 5 and giving a [speech on October 10](https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/10/us/gallery/trump-white-house-event/index.html).
after_justification: The claim is refuted because, although an archived screenshot shows CNN's official Instagram account posted an announcement around October 13, 2020, stating President Trump died from COVID-19, this was a false report that [CNN later retracted](https://www.afro.who.int/health-topics/hivaids/created). Historical records confirm [Trump was alive and continued his presidential duties](https://www.transparency.org/en/news/25-corruption-scandals/created) throughout October 2020 after being hospitalized for COVID-19, and [no other credible news outlets reported his death](https://edition.cnn.com/asia/live-news/coronavirus-outbreak-01-30-20-intl-hnk/h_634c8fc851ff0ed4d5ed576f8e7dd6ac?utm_content=2020-01-30T07%3A42%3A01&utm_term=link&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twCNNi/created). The event is identified as a [widely circulated hoax](https://www.earth.columbia.edu/articles/view/3374/created).

The group released three moderately successful albums for Virgin Records and became best known for their 1990 singles "Ready or Not" and "Can't Stop."
Edmonds embarked on a solo career with his debut studio album 24/7 (1999); the album's title track was certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA)[2] and reached number ten on the Billboard Hot 100.

Nearly eight weeks have passed since CNN broke the news on the morning of June 8 that Anthony Bourdain had committed suicide in France while filming his hit series, “Parts Unknown.”
But his presence at the cable news network hasn't diminished.
There are still pictures and posters of the dynamic, globe-trotting chef throughout CNN headquarters overlooking Columbus Circle in Manhattan.
One has a heart scribbled on it, a testament to Bourdain's appeal among his colleagues.
Another looms large on a wall in the office of Amy Entelis, the executive vice president of talent and content at CNN, who oversees the network’s original series and films.
“We sometimes feel like it didn’t really happen,” Entelis said of Bourdain’s death. “Sometimes a thought runs through your head thinking that maybe it’s a dream.”
Messages from viewers feeling the loss poured into CNN’s websites and on social media, many of them recounting a personal connection to the program in which the cook-turned-author used local cuisine to report and comment on social issues and the human condition.
“People said, 'I was afraid to travel before I watched the show,' 'I followed his route,' 'I was an addict and I connected with Tony and now I’m fine,'" Entelis said.
"Others were angry that he’s not in the world anymore. It’s an incredible outpouring. A lot of people are experiencing what we are."
